summary: Atsuyoshi Keika works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He held posts at Otani University, attested as a lecturer in 1990 and as a professor in 2014.

August Boeckh was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg under Wolf and Schleiermacher (c. 1803–1806). He taught at Grauen Kloster (1806–1807), Heidelberg (1807–1811), and the University of Berlin (1811–1861; Humboldt c. 1810–1867).

August Conrady specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Würzburg and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig. He held posts at Leipzig University from 1891 (becoming Ordinariat in 1922) and taught at Peking University (1903–1904).

August Fick was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (1852–1856). He later served as an extraordinary professor at Göttingen (1876) and full professor at the University of Breslau (1887–1891).

August Fischer worked in linguistics. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from c. 1884 to 1889. He held a post at Leipzig University from c. 1900 to 1930 and was a board member of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft in 1910.

August Friedrich Pott was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Franz Bopp. After lecturing in Berlin, he spent his career at Halle-Wittenberg as professor of general linguistics from 1833 and ordentlicher Professor from 1838.

August Hermann Francke worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Lehrerseminar Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and Humboldt University of Berlin (Habilitation c. 1921–1922), where he became a Privatdozent in 1922 and an extraordinary professor in 1925.

August Hjalmar Edgren was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Yale, Lund, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and served as Rector of the University of Gothenburg (1891–1893).

August Johan Bernet Kempers worked in archaeology, history, and Indology. After studying at Leiden University (c. 1924–1933), he served as director of Dinas Purbakala (c. 1947–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He taught at Göttingen and Jena before his long professorship at Leipzig University (1870, 1876–1915).

August Schleicher was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others. He held academic posts at Bonn (1846), Charles University (from 1850), and the University of Jena (1857).
August Sundin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been active at Ghent University as a PhD student and faculty member, both attested in 2026.

August Tholuck was a scholar of religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from c. 1816 to 1820, held a post there from c. 1820 to 1826, and later served at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from c. 1826 to 1877.

August Wilhelm von Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Göttingen under Heyne and Bürger, and later under Chézy and Hamilton. He became a professor at Jena (1798) and held the first chair of Indology at Bonn (1818).

Auguste Barth was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his licence at the University of Strasbourg (c. 1853–1856). He taught at Collège de Saverne (c. 1856–1861) and was a member of the Institut de France.
Auguste Comte was a philosopher. He was educated at the Lycée Joffre until 1814 and subsequently studied at the École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Awadh Kishore Narain worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at SOAS. He held major chairs and directorships at Banaras Hindu University and was professor at Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Axel Klein specializes in Japanology. He studied and worked at the University of Bonn, was a researcher at the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011), and was appointed professor of modern East Asian social studies at Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Hamburg and Kiel, and under Laxmi Nath Shrestha. He held posts at Kiel, Bern (1992–1996), and became professor of Classical Indology at Heidelberg University in 1996.

Ayako Nakamura-Walbeck specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Hamburg (attested 2009), where she also served as a research fellow (attested 2026).
